alignments.note: Vocative noun -> brethren. The Greek vocative is anarthrous, so no article competes and the ASV supplies no address word (rule 89's anarthrous clause); the possessive is s002's, not a supplied helper here.
Genitive pronoun realized by the possessive My. No article stands over the vocative, so rules 20 and 76 are not in question: the possessive is the pronoun's own.

Ordinary conditional ean -> if. Rule 72 is untouched: the particle does not stand after a relative or an indefinite pronoun generalizing it, so its closing clause applies and it is aligned to *if* like any other conditional.
Indefinite tis -> any. No negator stands in the clause, so rules 59 and 69 are not in question.

Aorist passive subjunctive rendered by the simple verb err; the ASV writes no auxiliary and no supplied subject, the subject being s004. Rule 36 keeps *from* off this verb even though *err from* reads as a phrasal unit in English.
Preposition apo -> from. Rule 36: the English preposition governing the phrase realizes the Greek preposition, not the verb it depends on.

Article -> the under rule 19. It takes a bare *the* and not *from the*: rule 21's case preposition rides with the article only where no Greek preposition is expressed, and apo is expressed here and takes *from* itself under rule 36.
Noun -> truth, standing bare beside its own article as rule 21 has it.
Expressed conjunction -> and. This is coordination the Greek writes, so rules 88 and 98 are not in question.
Subjunctive verb -> convert; the ASV writes no auxiliary. Rule 15 permits the reordering, the English subject *one* standing before the verb.
Second indefinite tis -> one, the subject of convert. Kept its own unit under rule 2 rather than merged with s012 or with the first tis at s004.
Accusative pronoun -> him, the object of convert.

review_notes: Reviewed unchanged: the accepted alignment is correct as it stands. All 14 source and 14 target ids are partitioned exactly once; every unit is aligned, with no unrepresented or added units in this verse, and every head is the sole token of a one-token unit under rule 10.

The verse is compositionally transparent and fully atomized: no source pair licenses a merge under rules 35, 39, 45 or 94, since the ASV writes a separate English word for every source token and no two tokens collapse into one.

s009 takes a bare *the* rather than *from the*. Rule 21 hands a case preposition to the article only where the Greek expresses no preposition; here apo is expressed and rule 36 keeps *from* on it, so the article anchors only the determiner and the noun stands bare.

s004 and s013 are the same lemma rendered two ways (*any*, *one*). Each is aligned to its own English word rather than merged into a shared unit; they are separate clause participants (the one who errs, and the one who converts him), so rule 24's same-analysis habit is satisfied by treating both as plain indefinites and not by giving them one unit.

Rule 36 is the only place this verse could plausibly have gone wrong: *err from* invites reading *from* as the verb's particle. The rule forbids it in terms, so *from* stays with apo and s007 keeps a bare *err*.
